status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly affirm the psychoacoustic findings, stating 'subjects are able to hear out a sequence of tones embedded in a complex acoustic environment' and that 'studies were appropriately performed with adequate controls.' The reviewers describe the segregation performance as 'remarkable,' particularly noting that 'segregation of the foreground tone sequence still occurs despite introduction of interleaved bursts of white noise between the foreground tones' with durations up to 500 ms.

Reviewers accept the interpretation about underlying mechanisms, stating 'these findings are clearly beyond the segregation capacities of core auditory cortex and the authors rightfully suggest non-classical auditory cortical processing stations as being the most likely generators of this percept.' This indicates reviewer agreement with claims about automatic segregation mechanisms and cortical involvement.

Reviewers implicitly support the inadequacy of adaptation-based models by affirming that 'the temporal coherence model is the most appropriate model for explaining how this foreground/background segregation develops.' This acceptance of temporal coherence as the appropriate framework implies agreement that adaptation-based models are insufficient for these complex stimuli.

While reviewers state that 'the temporal coherence model is the most appropriate model for explaining how this foreground/background segregation develops,' they express disappointment 'by the integration between data and modeling' and request that 'model simulations are not shown for all experimental manipulations.' This indicates the reviewers find the temporal coherence framework promising but want more comprehensive model-data comparison before fully endorsing the claims about model consistency.

Reviewers request clarification about experimental manipulations, asking 'what would their model predict for the manipulation?' and specifically noting 'it would be nice to see what the model predicts for the ramped SFG.' This indicates uncertainty about the interpretation of the ramped figure experiments and whether the temporal coherence model adequately accounts for these findings.
